handling_rule: Secret values are intentionally omitted from this artifact and must never be copied into governance, logs, issues or chat.

findings.evidence_scope: Repository search proves these tracked files contain plaintext login/password export material for multiple external services.
findings.interpretation: Every credential contained in these files must be treated as exposed to all principals with repository/history access, regardless of repository visibility.
immediate_non_destructive_actions: Do not print or copy any credential values.
Identify owning providers/accounts and rotate/revoke externally.
Prevent new browser-password exports from being committed.
Prepare current-tree removal and history remediation as separate governed actions.
blockers: Provider-side credential rotation cannot be achieved by a Git-only cleanup.
History rewrite is destructive/cross-clone and must not be performed implicitly.
Deleting files from current HEAD alone does not revoke exposed credentials or erase prior Git history.

findings.evidence_scope: The same third-party FX API credential is embedded in both the active monolith route and the inactive reference-service scaffold. Secret value intentionally omitted.
findings.interpretation: The active monolith exposes GET /api/fetch-currency-pairs without authentication; the route performs an external FX fetch and writes rows via devisedechanges.bulkCreate. This is both credential exposure and an HTTP GET-with-side-effect.
findings.runtime_note: src/routes/routes_vl.js is mounted by current app.js and is production-relevant. services/reference remains inactive scaffold and must not be treated as the authority.
immediate_non_destructive_actions: Do not print or copy the inline credential value.
Treat the provider credential as exposed and rotate/revoke it externally.
Do not call /api/fetch-currency-pairs as a test because it mutates the database.
Confirm the canonical FX ingestion path (current scheduled scripts/import/scrape_forex_import.js) before deprecating/removing the legacy HTTP writer.
Replace any future provider credential with environment/secret authority, never an inline literal.
blockers: Credential rotation is provider-side and cannot be completed by Git cleanup alone.
Removing the active route requires consumer audit and a bounded regression test.
Deleting the literal does not revoke the already-exposed provider credential.

governance_links.caveat: Do not assume AF-TASK-010 currently enumerates every provider credential in the password exports. Reconcile scope after queue ownership is released rather than creating a parallel secret queue.

promotion_candidate.title: Repository credential exposure remediation
phases: Inventory exposed provider/account owners without reproducing values.
Rotate/revoke every still-valid exposed provider credential out-of-band.
Prove the canonical scheduled FX importer covers required runtime behavior.
Disable or deprecate unauthenticated GET-with-write FX route through a governed code task; preserve read-only FX consumers.
Move any still-needed provider key to environment/secret authority.
Add ignore/pre-commit/secret-scan controls for browser credential exports and high-risk upload patterns.
Remove plaintext credential-export files from current tree after retention/evidence review.
Decide separately whether Git history rewrite is required; coordinate clones/deployments if approved.
done_when: No plaintext credential export remains in current tracked tree.
All still-valid exposed credentials are rotated/revoked by their providers.
Repository scanning gate prevents equivalent reintroduction.
No runtime regression from legacy credential removal.

next_action: Treat SEC-DISC-001 and SEC-DISC-002 as P0 security discovery. Reconcile them with AF-INTAKE-CAND-020 / AF-TASK-010 after queue release; provider rotation remains required independently of Git cleanup.
